summary:
Beep beep... Welcome aboard BUSSY 67! — Ghost Relics of the Solar System, an interactive 3D scrollytelling adventure that brings forgotten space explorers to life. Designed for school-age learners and casual space enthusiasts, it follows a friendly animated school bus on a journey beyond Earth.

Across 13 cinematic scenes, BUSSY visits the Moon and Mars, meeting Eagle, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP, Surveyor 3, Opportunity, Spirit, InSight, Pathfinder and Sojourner. On its return journey, BUSSY encounters the Kepler Space Telescope. Each machine becomes a character while retaining its recognizable design and mission identity.

Through narration, captions, 3D models, real imagery, sound and video portals, visitors discover why these machines were sent, how they worked and what humanity learned from their missions.

Instead of simply listing abandoned equipment, BUSSY 67! gives these silent explorers a voice, weaving their stories into an adventure about curiosity, ingenuity and discovery. Interactive environments and cinematic transitions make complex space science more approachable and engaging. The journey reminds us that even when machines are left behind, their contributions continue to shape our understanding of the Solar System—and inspire humanity's next steps into space.
details:
BUSSY 67! — Ghost Relics of the Solar System

Project Overview

BUSSY 67! is an interactive, 3D scrollytelling educational website that brings forgotten space-exploration hardware to life through a cinematic, character-driven adventure. Guided by BUSSY, a friendly animated school bus, visitors travel across the Solar System to meet the robotic explorers and scientific equipment left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

How It Works

The experience unfolds through 13 interconnected scenes controlled by scrolling. Take your time, relax, grab some Tacos and Prime, have your seat, get into the project's website on your device, click "Let's Start Exploring" on your screen, and scroll down smoothly as BUSSY travels from Earth to the Moon, explores historic lunar equipment, continues to Mars to encounter robotic explorers, and eventually journeys home. Along the way, visitors meet the Apollo 11 Lunar Module's descent stage (Eagle), the Lunar Roving Vehicle, ALSEP, Surveyor 3, Opportunity, Spirit, InSight, Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner, as well as the Kepler Space Telescope.

Each machine is brought to life as a friendly character while preserving its recognizable engineering design. Narration, educational captions, 3D models, real imagery, sound effects, background audio, and embedded video portals help explain each object's original purpose, operation, mission history, and scientific contributions.

Benefits and Intended Impact

The project makes space science more approachable for school-aged learners and casual space enthusiasts. Instead of presenting disconnected facts, it connects engineering, exploration, and scientific discoveries through an engaging narrative. It encourages curiosity about robotics, astronomy, planetary science, and the history of space exploration. Most importantly, it helps audiences appreciate that equipment left behind is not forgotten: its scientific legacy continues to contribute to humanity's understanding of the Solar System.

Creativity and Innovation

Our distinctive approach is to turn silent machines into storytellers. By combining animated personalities with recognizable real-world hardware, the experience creates an emotional connection between visitors and the technology that made exploration possible. The cinematic environments, scroll-driven camera movements, transitions between planets, and interactive information portals transform a conventional educational website into an immersive journey.

Technology and Development

Every code and assets are stored inside the GitHub repository, which can be accessed within the project's interface. The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Three.js for real-time 3D environments and model rendering, GSAP and ScrollTrigger for scroll-controlled animation, and Lenis for smooth scrolling. GLB 3D models, optimized 3D assets using Meshopt, the YouTube IFrame Player API, and locally hosted media support the interactive experience. The project is hosted live on Netlify with Porkbun domain registrar. Development involved desktop and mobile testing to improve accessibility, responsiveness, and performance. With helps of our very smart Artificial/Super Intelligence such as ChatGPT(Agentic coding and consulting), Gemini(2D image creation), Tripo(3D model creation), 11 Labs(Audio narration), Google Vids(Demo video), Google Omni(ALSEP and other videos), and some more, we leveraged our workflow and boosted the experience of the project too.

Design Considerations

We considered the intended audience, scientific accuracy, readability, visual clarity, accessibility, responsive design, loading performance, and the balance between entertainment and education. 2D images are reserved as fallback, in case 3D models don't load in the browser. Mission information and historical context guide the storytelling, while the friendly visual style helps make complex technology less intimidating.

BUSSY 67! ultimately celebrates the explorers that helped humanity reach farther, see deeper, and understand more about our Solar System. Their journeys may have ended, but their stories have not.
